chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Sinān, from Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān and Khalaf ibn Ḥammād, from Ribʿī ibn ʿAbd Allāh, from al-Fuḍayl ibn Yasār, from Abū ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

If a man takes from date-palms and cultivated crops before they are harvested, then there is no cutting upon him. But when the date-palms have been harvested and he takes, and when the crop has been reaped and he takes, his hand is cut.

key_terms.قَطْعٌ: the legal punishment of cutting the hand for theft
key_terms.يُصْرَمَ: to be harvested or cut from the date-palms

ai.seo_question: When is the hadd punishment for stealing dates or crops applied in Islamic law?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning theft from produce before and after harvest. It distinguishes between taking from palms and crops prior to collection, for which the hadd punishment is not applied, and taking after harvesting or reaping, for which the punishment of cutting applies.
